heroHeadline: PLA 7 Sorties (5 Cross Median Line, N/SW) on May 11; US Congress Urges Lai Visit Rights and Arms Sales Before Summit; Trump-Xi Beijing Meeting 3 Days Away
heroSubtitle: PLA posted 7 aircraft sorties on May 11, 2026 — 5 of 7 crossing the Taiwan Strait median line into northern and southwestern ADIZ sectors, with 5 PLAN vessels and 1 official ship — a moderate pullback from May 10's 12-sortie re-escalation but maintaining consistent median-line violations as the Trump-Xi Beijing summit approaches in 3 days (May 14-15). The full May pre-summit sortie sequence now reads: 4 (May 1) → 29 record (May 2) → 1 (May 3) → 2 (May 4) → 1 (May 5) → 0 (May 6) → 22 (May 7) → 12 (May 8) → 8 (May 9) → 12 (May 10) → 7 (May 11). On the diplomatic front, US Representatives Tom Tiffany (R-WI) and Chris Smith (R-NJ) sent a letter to Secretary Rubio on May 11 urging that President Lai Ching-te be granted the same US visit rights under the Taiwan Travel Act as KMT Chair Cheng Li-wun — who visited Washington in April. Senators Shaheen (D-NH) and Tillis (R-NC) separately pressed Trump to formally proceed with the pre-approved $14B arms package (PAC-3 MSE, NASAMS, integrated battle command system, loitering munitions) before departing for Beijing. The Washington Post and US News/AP published major summit-stakes analyses on May 11 confirming Xi Jinping will press Trump to limit arms sales to Taiwan and oppose independence, while Trump may use the arms pipeline as a diplomatic bargaining chip — a red line for bipartisan Congress. CNBC reported world leaders from Singapore to Brussels are monitoring the summit for Taiwan and Strait of Hormuz implications. The HIMARS down-payment deadline is now 20 days away (May 31), and the $14B PAC-3/NASAMS package remains on hold pending the summit outcome.
